The now hot HTF from the sulfur thermal storage will be used in commercially available shell and tube HTF heat exchanger to generate process steam for industrial facilities (Figure 2). The arrangement of pipes and the flow of HTF in the pipe circuit were optimized to maximize system efficiency based on experimental and computational understanding of molten sulfur natural convection dynamics. Project Objectives The overall goal of the project is to advance the design and development of molten sulfur thermal energy storage (TES) product to a manufacturing-relevant prototype stage for solar industrial process heat applications, while establishing and validating a realistic pathway to commercial success. The primary challenge with adoption of solar thermal is solar intermittency that reduces the capacity factor of solar thermal systems, decreases its reliability to supply continuous and on-demand heat, and increases levelized cost of heat (LCOH). The proposed development of low-cost molten sulfur TES for integration with solar thermal will increase system resiliency to provide on-demand/continuous heat supply and reduce levelized cost of heat from solar thermal to the point that it is competitive with natural gas-based thermal equipment. The project will have the following positive impacts: Economic development and Environmental benefits: The successful development of technology will improve US manufacturing economic competitiveness by reducing natural gas purchases for process heat. Reducing natural gas usage will reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and benefit the environment.
